text:
Security Policy and Architectural Constraints for Logic Flaw Prevention:
1. Server-Side State Verification: Explicitly validate all preconditions, invariants, and postconditions on the server prior to state advancement.
2. Non-relying Input Validation: Do not depend on client-side constraints; validate domain-level sanity of all incoming values before processing.
3. Workflow Invariant Enforcement: Maintain strict transactional state machines where transitions require cryptographic or session-bound proof of prior step completion.
4. Architectural Dependency Auditing: Formally model side effects between integrated services to prevent out-of-order cross-component execution.

metadata.title: Defensive Guidelines for Logic-Safe System Design
metadata.policy_scope: API Gateways, Workflow Orchestrators, State Machine Engines
metadata.enforcement_layer: Server-side controllers and domain model services

rule_constraints.invariant: All workflow transitions must explicitly verify completion of prerequisite states
rule_constraints.precondition: Input values must pass domain boundary and semantic integrity checks
rule_constraints.postcondition: Terminal states must transition atomically to prevent state re-entry

text: Authoritative Server-Side Pricing Invariant: Financial values such as item price, discount calculations, and currency rates must strictly originate from authoritative server-side storage or database lookups. Endpoints accepting user submissions for cart management must accept only product identifiers (e.g., product_id, quantity) and forbid client-controllable price parameters.

metadata.title: Server-Side Authoritative Pricing Enforcement

rule_constraints.invariant: order.total == sum(item.quantity * catalog.getPrice(item.id) for item in cart.items)
rule_constraints.precondition: All product pricing must resolve via internal catalog mapping at runtime

text: Cart Item Quantity Policy and Invariants: All transactional endpoints accepting product quantities must enforce domain-level input validation ensuring the quantity is a strictly positive integer (quantity > 0 and quantity <= max_allowed_limit). Subtraction or item removal must use dedicated removal endpoints (e.g., DELETE /cart/items/{id}) rather than negative delta inputs. Invariant check: At no point may cart.items[i].quantity <= 0 or cart.total < sum(catalog_price(item) * item.qty).

metadata.title: Strict Positivity Invariant for Transactional Quantities
metadata.policy_scope: Order Management, Cart Services, Inventory Controllers

rule_constraints.invariant: all(item.quantity > 0 for item in cart.items) and cart.total >= 0
rule_constraints.precondition: input.quantity > 0 and isinstance(input.quantity, int)

text: Continuous Trust and Re-verification Policy Invariant: Any state mutation that updates identity or trust-determining attributes (such as email domain, company affiliation, or role) must enforce identical verification constraints across all application endpoints. If privilege derivation depends on domain validation, any update to that attribute must immediately revoke existing privileges and transition the account to an unverified state until domain ownership is re-proven via cryptographic or out-of-band verification.

metadata.title: Uniform Domain Validation and Re-Authentication Invariant

rule_constraints.invariant: user.is_admin == True iff user.email.domain == privileged_domain and user.email_verified == True
rule_constraints.precondition: All profile update endpoints must validate domain constraints and reset email_verified to False on address change
rule_constraints.postcondition: Privileged roles cannot be granted based on unverified, user-submitted identity strings

text: Stateful Discount Enforcement Invariant: A promotional discount code must be validated against a persistent, immutable set of all coupons applied to the active order (applied_coupons: Set[CouponID]), as well as historical user redemption records. Applying a coupon code requires that coupon_id not in order.applied_coupons and coupon.redemption_count < allowed_limit. Successive coupon applications must not overwrite or flush historical application tracking within the cart session.

metadata.title: Set-Based Unique Coupon Application Invariant

rule_constraints.invariant: len(order.applied_coupons) == len(set(order.applied_coupons)) and all(c.usage_per_order <= 1 for c in order.applied_coupons)
rule_constraints.precondition: submitted_coupon.id not in [c.id for c in order.applied_coupons]
rule_constraints.postcondition: order.total == max(0, catalog_total - sum(c.deduction for c in order.applied_coupons))

text: Safe Financial Arithmetic and Upper Bound Invariant: All financial aggregations, balance updates, and cart subtotal computations must employ overflow-safe math constructs (e.g., arbitrary-precision decimals, BigInteger, or language-level checked arithmetic). Systems must enforce upper saturation limits on line items and overall cart value before state persistence. Any operation that causes arithmetic overflow, underflow, or undefined numeric wrapping must immediately reject the state transition and terminate the transaction.

metadata.title: Arithmetic Bounds and Overflow-Safe Financial Accumulation

rule_constraints.invariant: cart.subtotal == sum(item.quantity * item.unit_price) and cart.subtotal <= MAX_SAFE_ORDER_LIMIT
rule_constraints.precondition: will_overflow(cart.subtotal, item.quantity * item.unit_price) == False
rule_constraints.postcondition: cart.subtotal >= 0 and type(cart.subtotal) is SafeDecimal

text: Uniform String Boundary and Sanitization Policy: All layers processing sensitive identity attributes (web validation controllers, messaging queues, SMTP dispatchers, and persistence layers) must enforce identical length and format constraints. Database column definitions must either support the full RFC standard length (RFC 5321 specifies up to 254 octets for path/reverse-path) or reject inputs exceeding constraints outright with an error rather than silently truncating. Invariant: Input validation length check must be less than or equal to database column capacity (MAX_INPUT_LENGTH <= DB_COLUMN_CAPACITY).

metadata.title: Uniform Field Length Validation and Fail-Closed Persistence Invariant

rule_constraints.invariant: stored_value == incoming_value and len(incoming_value) <= MAX_ALLOWED_COLUMN_WIDTH
rule_constraints.precondition: len(email) <= 254 and regex_match(rfc5322_email_pattern, email)
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject_transaction_if(len(raw_input) > column_limit)

text: Endpoint Segregation and Session Identity Binding Invariant: Privileged administrative overrides and self-service account modifications must be strictly decoupled into separate, role-gated endpoints (e.g., /admin/users/{id}/password vs /user/profile/password). Self-service identity state mutations must derive the target user context exclusively from the verified server-side session token, never from client-supplied request parameters. Endpoints requiring prior credential confirmation must enforce parameter presence and validity as a mandatory precondition before dispatching to lower-level services.

metadata.title: Strict Endpoint Separation and Non-Controllable Target Invariant

rule_constraints.invariant: target_user_id == session.authenticated_user_id unless session.has_explicit_admin_role() == True
rule_constraints.precondition: request.has_parameter('current-password') and verify_password(session.user, request.get('current-password'))
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject_request_if(request.contains('username') and not session.is_authorized_admin())

text: Stateful Workflow Transition Integrity Invariant: An application workflow represented by a Finite State Machine (FSM) must enforce strict sequence validation server-side. Terminal state execution ($S_{completed}$) must require verified, non-replayable, cryptographic or database-backed proof that all mandatory antecedent states ($S_{cart} \to S_{payment}$) transitioned successfully. Navigating to post-payment confirmation endpoints without an active, verified, and unconsumed payment token must terminate the session or return HTTP 400/403.

metadata.title: Strict State Sequence and Prerequisite State Verification Invariant

rule_constraints.invariant: state(order) == ORDER_CONFIRMED iff state(payment) == PAYMENT_CAPTURED and payment.order_id == order.id
rule_constraints.precondition: session.has_valid_payment_receipt_for(cart.active_id) == True
rule_constraints.postcondition: cart.transition_to(ORDER_CONFIRMED) and invalidate(session.payment_receipt)

text: Fail-Safe Defaults and Complete State Machine Invariant: In multi-step authentication and provisioning flows, the intermediate session state must default to minimum privilege (deny-all / uninitialized role). No access to protected application controllers must be granted until the final transition state ($S_{terminal}$) completes successfully and an explicit role assignment is confirmed. Premature termination or dropping of intermediate transitions must invalidate the intermediate session token rather than allowing access with unconstrained defaults.

metadata.title: Principle of Fail-Safe Defaults in Stateful Authentication Sequences

rule_constraints.invariant: session.role == 'ROLE_NONE' until state == 'AUTHENTICATION_COMPLETE'
rule_constraints.precondition: all(step in completed_steps for step in required_auth_steps) == True
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject_request_with_401_if(session.state != 'AUTHENTICATION_COMPLETE' and requested_resource.requires_auth)

text: Promotional Scope and Valuation Invariant: Promotional coupons, percentage discounts, and marketing vouchers must strictly exclude cash-equivalent products, gift cards, stored-value certificates, and currency transfers from eligible subtotal calculations. Precondition: For any item in order.items where item.is_cash_equivalent == True, item.discount_eligible must evaluate to False. Invariant: The acquisition price of a stored-value instrument must never be lower than its redeemable face value when purchased using the same currency denomination or store credit system.

metadata.title: Cash-Equivalent Discount Exclusion and Face Value Invariant

rule_constraints.invariant: gift_card.redeemable_value <= gift_card.settled_purchase_cost
rule_constraints.precondition: item.type == 'GIFT_CARD' implies coupon.is_applicable(item) == False
rule_constraints.postcondition: assert not (user_balance_delta > 0 after complete_transaction_cycle(cart, voucher_redemption))

text: Cryptographic Domain Separation and Authenticated Encryption Invariant: Cryptographic keys must never be shared across disparate application workflows or data sensitivity tiers. State tokens and encrypted cookies must enforce: 1) Unique, domain-separated subkeys derived via a Key Derivation Function (e.g., HKDF with explicit info contexts like 'auth-session-cookie' vs 'ui-notification'). 2) Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD, e.g., AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305) to detect any ciphertext tampering, byte truncation, or block splicing before decryption. Invariant: Ciphertext produced in context A must fail integrity verification and be rejected outright if consumed within context B.

metadata.title: Cryptographic Key Domain Separation and AEAD Integrity Invariant

rule_constraints.invariant: verify_aead_tag(ciphertext, key_domain, associated_data) == True
rule_constraints.precondition: context(sender) == context(receiver) and key_derivation_info == explicit_workflow_purpose
rule_constraints.postcondition: tampered_ciphertext_causes_fail_closed_exception()

text: Canonical Email Address Parsing and Single-Parser Invariant: All application layers—input filtering, authorization policy evaluation, database persistence, and message transmission/MTA handoff—must employ an identical, authoritative RFC 5321/5322 parsing engine operating on fully normalized and canonicalized strings. Decouple delivery addresses from identity assertions: domain validation for access control must be executed against the terminal mailbox host extracted post-MIME-decoding, never against raw, unnormalized, or composite input strings. All obsolete or non-standard charset encodings (including UTF-7, raw escape sequences, or unexpected RFC 2047 headers in local-part contexts) must fail closed at the API boundary.

metadata.title: Canonicalized Single-Parser Email Domain Invariant

rule_constraints.invariant: destination_mta_host == domain_policy_evaluated_host
rule_constraints.precondition: email.is_normalized() == True and has_unsupported_encodings(email) == False
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject_registration_if(parse_canonical_domain(decode_mime(email)) != authoritative_allowed_domain)

text: Email Domain Authorization and Single-Source Validation Policy: Never use email address domains as the sole means of authentication, authorization, or trust enforcement (such as verifying corporate identity or Cloudflare Zero Trust access gates), because email parsing standards, encodings, and legacy MTA behaviors allow arbitrary domain spoofing and splitting. Applications must disable encoded-word decoding within sensitive validation contexts or enforce strict regex validation (e.g., checking for '=[?].+[?]=') to reject non-standard MIME headers. All identities asserted via external Single Sign-On (SSO) providers or email channels must undergo continuous secondary verification.

metadata.title: Prohibition of Email Domain-Based Access Control and Defensive Normalization

rule_constraints.invariant: never_trust_email_domain_for_authorization() == True
rule_constraints.precondition: parse_email_address(input) must reject inputs matching '=[?].+[?]=', control characters, and unexpected Punycode malformations
rule_constraints.postcondition: enforce multi-factor verification independent of unvalidated email domain substrings

text: Policy and Invariants for Stateful Business Operations: 1) Strict State Traversal: The application state machine must enforce that state transition $S_n$ strictly requires validated completion of $S_{n-1}$. Unhandled transitions must fail closed (deny access). 2) Authoritative Pricing and Re-validation: Crucial parameters (e.g., price, quantity, roles) must be derived exclusively from server-side datastores and re-verified immediately prior to final settlement. 3) Resource Lock Lifecycles: Resource reservations must enforce bounded timeouts and atomic expiration controls to prevent denial-of-inventory or starvation attacks. 4) Transactional Rollback Atomicity: If a primary transaction state is cancelled or fails, all dependent side-effects (e.g., accrued reward points, store credits, voucher activations) must be atomically revoked within the same transactional boundary.

metadata.title: Stateful Transaction Integrity and Resource Reservation Policy

rule_constraints.state_transition_invariant: current_state == S_n iff prior_state == S_{n-1} and prerequisites_satisfied(S_{n-1}) == True
rule_constraints.pricing_invariant: order.billed_total == sum(item.quantity * catalog.price(item.id) for item in order.items)

text: Continuous Semantic Verification and Zero-Trust Inter-Service Handoff Policy: 1) Multi-Tier Validation Invariant: Every service, microservice, and downstream integration partner must independently validate the contextual and logical validity of incoming data before state progression. Data validated at the front-end or ingress gateway must never be treated as implicitly trustworthy across internal handoffs. 2) Authoritative State Verification: Transaction authorization must execute against real-time, authoritative server-side state rather than stale, cached, or batched data models. 3) Economic and Frequency Bound Invariants: Financial transfer endpoints must enforce minimum transaction thresholds and chargeback/fee caps to prevent asymmetric economic depletion (DDo$). Any transaction where transactional overhead exceeds transferred asset value must be blocked or routed to administrative approval.

metadata.title: Zero-Trust Data Handoff and Semantic Validity Invariant

rule_constraints.invariant: downstream_service.validate_semantics(payload) == True regardless of upstream_origin

text: Server-Side State Sovereignty and Production Debug Sanitization Policy: 1) Client State Distrust Invariant: Workflow control parameters (such as whether a discount has been claimed, user privilege tier, or workflow step completion) must be stored in tamper-proof server-side session stores or cryptographically signed state containers. They must never be accepted from client POST/GET parameters. 2) Debug Pipeline Exclusion: Development, debugging, and testing flags (such as test_mode, bypass_auth, debug) must be stripped from application binaries during production build pipelines. 3) Idempotency Invariant: Financial, gamification, and reward accrual operations must be strictly idempotent and validated against an immutable server-side audit log.

metadata.title: State Sovereignty and Production Hardening Policy

rule_constraints.invariant: order.discount_applied == True implies session.has_discount_record(order.id) == True
rule_constraints.precondition: assert not request.has_param_in(['debug', 'simulate', 'dry_run'])

text: Server-Side Relational Integrity and Authorization Policy: 1) Non-Editable Field Invariant: Values marked as read-only, static, or hidden in client interfaces must never be consumed from incoming HTTP payloads; authoritative values must resolve strictly from server-side session contexts or canonical databases. 2) Relational Scoping Invariant: When an operation references a relational entity key (e.g., project_id, account_id), the server must evaluate whether user.has_access(entity_id) is True before dispatching the query. 3) Multi-Field Referential Sanity: Relational updates must execute atomic validation rules ensuring all interrelated fields are mutually consistent (e.g., marital_status == 'single' enforces spouse_name == null). 4) Log Artifact Protection: Audit trails and system logs must enforce append-only policies, cryptographic tamper-evidence, and strict isolation preventing modification by application-tier users.

metadata.title: Server-Side Relational Edits and Immutable Audit Logging Invariant

rule_constraints.server_side_authority: assert not request.contains('role') if not session.is_admin()

text: Constant-Time Processing and Transactional TTL Policy: 1) Constant-Time Execution Invariant: Identity authentication, token comparison, and cryptographic operations must execute within uniform time bounds regardless of parameter validity or lookup outcome, using dummy hashing operations on invalid accounts to normalize execution duration. 2) Strict Reservation Lifecycles: Any state transition placing exclusive locks on shared resources (e.g., inventory, seat allocations) must enforce an immutable Time-To-Live (e.g., $TTL \le 300s$), rolling back automatically on timeout. 3) Price Quote Freshness Invariant: Time-sensitive quotes must enforce explicit validity ceilings; checkout execution must assert $T_{current} - T_{quote} \le MaxQuoteDuration$, requiring mandatory re-quote and client acknowledgement upon expiration.

metadata.title: Constant-Time Verification and Transaction Expiration Invariant

text: Database-Backed Invocation Quota and Atomicity Policy: Functions linked to financial discounts, asset downloads, or operational rewards must enforce hard, database-backed atomic checks (e.g., conditional atomic updates or distributed locks). Precondition: Invocations must verify $user.usage\_count < quota.limit$ and assert that promotional tokens are in state 'ACTIVE'. Postcondition: Coupon status must transition to 'REDEEMED' or user counters must atomically increment prior to returning execution success. State resets must never be derived from client-driven navigation.

metadata.title: Atomic Quota Enforcement and Database-Level Lock Invariant

text: Workflow State Transition Integrity and Transactional Atomicity Invariant: 1) Atomic Settlement Invariant: Auxiliary benefits, reward allocations, and state elevations tied to a commercial transaction must not be finalized until payment settlement is confirmed; if the workflow aborts or tenders an altered amount, dependent assets must atomically roll back within the same transactional boundary. 2) Symmetric Lifecycle Validation: All validation policies, business rules, and constraints applied during entity creation must be applied equivalently to all modification, update, and append endpoints. 3) Strict Sequence Enforcement: State machines must enforce that transition $S_n$ is accepted only if verified, non-reusable proof of completion for state $S_{n-1}$ is present in the server-managed session context.

metadata.title: Transactional Atomicity and Symmetric Lifecycle Policy

rule_constraints.lifecycle_symmetry: validate_content(post.content) on update == validate_content(post.content) on create

text: Application-Layer Active Self-Defense and Misuse Containment Policy: Applications must implement holistic runtime misuse detection (e.g., OWASP AppSensor architecture). Invariants: 1) Anomaly Thresholding: A single authenticated session accumulating repeated business logic violations, access control failures, parameter duplications, or out-of-order state transitions within a moving time window must trigger an automated escalation policy. 2) Tiered Remediation Response: Minor misuse thresholds must enforce progressive request delays (tarpitting) or step-up authentication; critical misuse thresholds must immediately revoke the active session, lock the account, and emit high-priority security telemetry. 3) Contextual Telemetry: Security incident logs must record sanitized headers, payload structures, and state history upon detection of anomalous traversal patterns.

metadata.title: Application-Aware Self-Defense and Misuse Escalation Invariant

rule_constraints.misuse_escalation: if session.misuse_score >= CRITICAL_THRESHOLD: session.terminate() and account.lock()

text: Secure File Upload and Ingestion Policy: 1) Strict Extension Allowlist Invariant: Upload handlers must enforce a strict, definitive allowlist of permitted extensions derived strictly from business requirements; all unapproved extensions must be rejected fail-closed. 2) Multi-Tier Validation: File validation must inspect the file extension, verify the declared MIME type, and validate the internal content using magic byte / binary header inspection. 3) Storage Isolation and Renaming Invariant: Uploaded files must be renamed to randomly generated UUIDs, stripped of execution privileges (stored on non-executable mounts or S3/blob stores), and served exclusively with 'Content-Disposition: attachment' or under an isolated sandbox domain. 4) Archive Path Normalization: Decompression utilities must canonicalize internal file paths and reject any entry resolving outside the target destination root.

metadata.title: File Ingestion Validation, Storage Isolation, and Extension Allowlist Policy

text: Malicious File Upload Defense, Content Scanning, and Storage Isolation Policy: 1) Anti-Malware Pipeline Invariant: Every uploaded file stream must be scanned by automated antimalware/antivirus engines before persistence; infected or unrecognized executable payloads must be quarantined immediately. 2) Execution Neutralization Invariant: Uploaded files must never be saved within the web server execution root; storage must use non-executable dedicated object stores (e.g., S3 buckets, dedicated storage mounts with noexec flags). 3) Safe Archive Extraction: Archive extraction utilities must canonicalize internal file paths and abort if any entry resolves outside the designated sandbox root; decompression limits must cap maximum extracted byte volume and nesting depth. 4) Active Content Stripping: Permitted media and documents must be re-encoded or sanitized (e.g., stripping EXIF metadata, re-rendering images via graphics libraries) to neutralize embedded polyglots or malicious script tags.

metadata.title: Malicious File Upload Scanning, Isolation, and Archive Handling Invariant

rule_constraints.archive_traversal_check: assert not any('..' in entry.filename or entry.is_absolute() for entry in archive.entries)

text: Defensive Invariants and Architectural Enforcement Policy: 1) Server-Side Value Derivation: All security-sensitive attributes (prices, totals, taxes, discounts, user roles, resource ownership) must be recomputed and derived exclusively from authoritative server databases; client-supplied values must be treated as untrusted inputs. 2) Explicit Finite State Machine Enforcement: Multi-step processes must be represented as persistent server-side state machines keyed to session tokens; transitions must assert strict predecessor completion, reject step replays, and expire incomplete states after a finite TTL. 3) Atomic Operations: Critical check-then-act sequences must execute inside serialized database transactions, explicit row locks (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), or conditional updates (UPDATE ... WHERE balance >= amount) to prevent race conditions. 4) Feature-Level Quotas and Idempotency: All value-dispensing operations must enforce per-action and per-account caps, feature-specific rate limits, and caller-scoped idempotency keys.

metadata.title: Server-Side Derivation, State Machine, and Concurrency Defense Policy

rule_constraints.atomic_decrement: UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - :amount WHERE id = :id AND balance >= :amount

text: Root-Cause Granularity and Business Logic Mapping Policy: Security classification and automated triage engines must not use CWE-840 as a leaf vulnerability label in vulnerability repositories, test logs, or findings reports. Any business logic flaw detected during runtime analysis or manual testing must be decomposed into its root-cause functional failure mode. Violations governing sequence order and state skipping must map to CWE-841 (Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow); multi-spend, coupon replay, and single-use bypasses must map to CWE-837 (Improper Enforcement of a Single, Unique Action); resource consumption and flooding must map to CWE-770 (Allocation of Resources Without Limits); and parameter tampering on identity handles must map to CWE-639 (User-Controlled Key Authorization Bypass).

metadata.title: Mandatory Granular Root-Cause Mapping Policy for CWE-840

rule_constraints.postcondition: record.root_cause != 'Business Logic Error' and record.root_cause != ''

text: Strict State Sequence and Behavioral Workflow Integrity Policy: Multi-step transactional workflows must be implemented as formal, server-side Finite State Machines (FSM). Invariants: 1) State Monotonicity & Prerequisites: Transition to state S_n is valid if and only if state S_{n-1} was successfully executed and validated in the active server session context. 2) Fail-Closed Step Verification: Any request arriving out of sequence, skipping prerequisite stages, or exceeding allowable execution time windows must immediately invalidate the workflow state and terminate the session. 3) Anti-Replay: Completed operational steps must be marked non-replayable using cryptographically signed, single-use transition nonces.

metadata.title: Server-Side Finite State Machine and Sequence Enforcement Invariant

rule_constraints.sequence_integrity: can_transition(S_n) == True iff session.current_state == S_{n-1} and prerequisites_met(S_{n-1})
rule_constraints.postcondition: on_sequence_violation_abort_and_rollback()

text: Atomic Resource Evaluation and Concurrency Synchronization Invariant: Critical sections operating on shared resources, financial balances, quotas, or single-use state tokens must eliminate non-atomic check-then-act patterns. State verification and state mutation must occur within a single atomic database operation (e.g., conditional atomic updates: UPDATE ... SET balance = balance - :amount WHERE id = :id AND balance >= :amount) or within an isolated transaction enforcing pessimistic row-level locking (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE). Locks must be acquired prior to the check to guarantee the evaluated resource state remains immutable until the transaction commits.

metadata.title: Pessimistic Locking and Atomic State Mutation Invariant

rule_constraints.invariant: resource_state_at_use == resource_state_at_check

text: Persistent Action Uniqueness and Idempotency Invariant: Operations designed as single-use or unique per entity must enforce uniqueness server-side using durable database constraints (e.g., UNIQUE (actor_id, action_id, target_entity_id)). Invariants: 1) Strict Cardinality Check: An action execution record must satisfy count(actions where actor_id == user.id and target == resource.id) <= 1. 2) Client State Distrust: Proof of prior execution must never rely on client-controllable indicators such as cookies, query parameters, or localStorage. 3) Transactional Finality: State transitions recording completion of single-use operations must commit atomically before any dependent assets, votes, or rewards are dispatched.

metadata.title: Database-Enforced Uniqueness and Single-Action Invariant

rule_constraints.precondition: assert not exists(SELECT 1 FROM action_audit_log WHERE actor_id = :actor_id AND action_type = :type AND target_id = :target_id)
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject_action_with_409_conflict_if_duplicate()

text: Deterministic Control Flow and Behavioral Integrity Policy: 1) Canonicalization Precedence Invariant: All input decoding, normalization, and canonicalization must execute prior to input validation and access control evaluation (Canonicalize -> Authenticate/Authorize -> Execute). 2) Terminal Execution on Redirect: Any control block executing an HTTP redirection due to authorization or validation failure must invoke an immediate, deterministic program termination (e.g., exit() / return) to prevent Execution After Redirect (EAR). 3) Granular Root-Cause Mapping Mandate: Automated security checkers, static analysis parsers, and triage tools must not assign findings to CWE-438; defects must be categorized under the leaf failure mode (e.g., CWE-551 for path normalization issues, CWE-698 for EAR, CWE-841 for workflow order).

metadata.title: Canonicalization Ordering and Fail-Closed Execution Invariant

rule_constraints.redirection_atomicity: http_redirect() must immediately be followed by exit_process()

text: Interaction Frequency Governance and Anti-Automation Invariant: All endpoints performing state mutations, computational evaluations, authentication challenges, or value-dispensing operations must enforce multi-layered rate-limiting and anti-automation controls. Invariants: 1) Velocity Ceiling Invariant: Incoming requests per identity key (session ID, user UID, API key, and client fingerprint) must not exceed defined threshold limits: requests(identity_key, window_t) <= MAX_ALLOWED_REQUESTS. 2) Layered Context Throttling: Rate limits must be applied at the specific feature level, not merely at network ingress gateways. 3) Fail-Closed Backpressure: Upon exceeding frequency bounds, the backend must immediately throttle interactions by returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, requiring challenge-response proofs (e.g., CAPTCHAs), or applying exponential backoff delay multipliers.

metadata.title: Multi-Layered Anti-Automation and Feature-Level Rate Limiting Policy

text: Control Flow Management and Explicit Synchronization Policy: 1) Checked Synchronization Invariant: Every synchronization primitive (mutex, distributed lock, transaction begin) must explicitly evaluate its return status before entering a critical section; failure to acquire a lock must immediately abort execution. 2) Authorization Prior to Processing: Authorization gates and access validation must execute before resource-intensive operations, file reads, or external API handoffs (Authorize -> Retrieve -> Render). 3) Explicit Block Scoping: All conditional branches and loop constructs must use explicit code block delimitations regardless of single-statement brevity. 4) Pillar Mapping Rule: Static analysis tools and automated classifiers must decompose CWE-691 alerts into actionable child classes (CWE-841, CWE-799, CWE-696, CWE-705) prior to persistence.

metadata.title: Rigorous Control Flow Verification and Synchronization Handling Invariant

text: Strict Execution Precedence and Canonicalization Pipeline Policy: 1) Canonicalization First Invariant: Input strings, paths, and URIs must undergo complete decoding, normalization, and canonicalization before input validation rules, allowlists, or access control policies are evaluated (Canonicalize -> Validate -> Authorize -> Execute). 2) Authorization Before Ingestion: Authorization gates must execute and succeed before reading large files into memory, initiating heavy database queries, or dispatching external API requests. 3) Correct Privilege Revocation: System privilege drops must follow strict POSIX ordering: group privileges must be revoked (setgid) before dropping user privileges (setuid), with return codes checked explicitly. 4) Taxonomic Mapping Mandate: Triage engines should evaluate base-level children (CWE-179, CWE-551, CWE-1280) when classifying concrete vulnerability instances under CWE-696.

metadata.title: Canonicalization-First and Authorization Precedence Invariant

text: Deterministic Termination and Control Flow Scoping Policy: 1) Fail-Closed Immediate Termination: Every conditional branch detecting an authorization violation, authentication error, or required HTTP redirect must terminate script/handler execution immediately via deterministic exit constructs (e.g., return, exit(), or throwing a terminating SecurityException). Control flow must never fall through to subsequent business logic or data retrieval operations. 2) Container Safe Exit Invariant: Shared application code executing within servlet containers, application servers, or async workers must never invoke process-level termination (e.g., System.exit()) inside exception catch blocks. 3) Controlled Error Scoping: Exceptions must be caught at specific granular boundaries rather than generic global handlers, preventing unexpected state preservation or incomplete database transaction scopes.

metadata.title: Immediate Control Flow Termination and Error Scoping Invariant

rule_constraints.redirect_termination_invariant: assert redirect_call() is immediately followed by return_statement

text: Authentication Attempt Restriction and Lockout Invariant: 1) Failed Attempt Thresholds: Authentication endpoints must enforce a strict, centralized limit on consecutive failed login attempts (e.g., failed_attempts <= MAX_ATTEMPTS within sliding window T); exceeding this limit must temporarily lock the target account or suspend login capabilities for that identity. 2) Global and Per-Identity Concurrency Bounds: Rate limiting must enforce limits per target username and per client IP/fingerprint to resist distributed dictionary spraying and multi-threaded parallel connection attacks. 3) Cryptographic Proof-of-Work / Challenge-Response: Following initial failed attempts, subsequent requests must mandate progressive interactive challenges (e.g., CAPTCHA, step-up MFA, or client puzzle computation) before backend credential evaluation executes.

metadata.title: Adaptive Lockout, Concurrency Bound, and Anti-Automation Invariant

text: SDLC Taxonomy Organization and Granular Mapping Policy: 1) View Mapping Prohibition: Automated analyzers, triaging scripts, and vulnerability databases must enforce an invariant prohibiting CWE-699 from being used as a root-cause identifier ($assert\ finding.cwe\ != 'CWE-699'$). 2) Lifecycle Phase Alignment: Security weaknesses discovered during architectural threat modeling, design reviews, static analysis, or dynamic penetration testing must be traced through CWE-699's functional categories down to specific Base or Variant weakness nodes. 3) Domain Partitioning: Flaws involving business workflow, multi-step ordering, or access enforcement must navigate from CWE-699 into designated subcategories (such as CWE-840, CWE-1212, or CWE-1217) and resolve to actionable leaf weaknesses (e.g., CWE-841, CWE-837, CWE-639).

metadata.title: Taxonomic SDLC Categorization and View Mapping Prohibition

rule_constraints.decomposition_requirement: finding.cwe_category in CWE_699_CATEGORIES and finding.cwe_type in ['Base', 'Variant', 'Class']

text: Secure Design Principles and Threat Modeling Policy (CWE-1348): 1) Server-Side Authority Invariant: All security-critical calculations, authorization states, and business parameters (prices, privileges, roles, ownership, workflow states) must be derived and verified authoritatively on the server; client input must be treated strictly as unverified request data (assert not trust_client_state). 2) Explicit Finite State Machine Enforcement: Multi-step workflows must enforce strict state transitions in server-managed storage, rejecting out-of-order invocations fail-closed. 3) Trust Boundary Isolation: Untrusted external inputs must undergo canonicalization, structural validation, and privilege sanitization before crossing into trusted internal service buses or session stores. 4) Grouping Mapping Prohibition: Static and dynamic triage pipelines must not output CWE-1348 as a leaf finding; all insecure design defects must map to specific underlying base weaknesses (e.g., CWE-602, CWE-807, CWE-841, CWE-799).

metadata.title: Secure Design Invariants, Trust Boundary Integrity, and Mapping Rules

text: Security invariant: every object access must resolve the authenticated principal and evaluate ownership or explicit delegation on the server before any read, mutation, or deletion. Precondition: the request carries a validated session and a resource identifier. Postcondition: if resource.owner_id != principal.id and no active delegation grant exists, the operation fails closed with 403 or 404 without disclosing object existence. Enforcement must be centralized in a policy layer or repository query scoped by tenant_id and owner_id, not duplicated in controllers. Administrative overrides require a separate, audited capability.

metadata.title: CWE-283 Security Invariant: Unverified Resource Ownership

rule_constraints.invariant: resource.owner_id == principal.id or delegation_exists(principal, resource)
rule_constraints.precondition: principal is authenticated and resource_id resolves to an existing object
rule_constraints.postcondition: access denied unless ownership or explicit delegation is proven server-side

text: Security invariant: object authorization is evaluated against the resolved object, never against the route alone. Precondition: the principal is authenticated and the object key is resolved to a record. Postcondition: the record must belong to the principal tenant and owner, or the principal must hold an explicit capability; otherwise the response is a uniform 404 or 403. Data access layers should enforce tenant scoping by default so that a forgotten predicate fails closed. Object keys must never be trusted as proof of entitlement, and batch or nested lookups must apply the same check to every element.

metadata.title: CWE-639 Security Invariant: IDOR and Object Key Substitution

rule_constraints.invariant: lookup(object_key).tenant_id == principal.tenant_id and (object.owner_id == principal.id or principal.has_capability(object))
rule_constraints.precondition: principal is authenticated and object_key resolves server-side
rule_constraints.postcondition: 404 or 403 on mismatch with no existence disclosure; every query is tenant- and owner-scoped

text: Security invariant: a recovery token is a single-use, short-lived, account-bound capability that is compared in constant time. Precondition: the recovery request is bound to a verified channel owned by the account, and the reset link host is fixed by server configuration rather than request headers. Postcondition: the token is invalidated atomically on first use, no password change occurs without a valid unexpired token, and responses for known and unknown accounts are indistinguishable. Throttling and lockout apply per account and per source, and recovery events are audited.

metadata.title: CWE-640 Security Invariant: Password Recovery Abuse

rule_constraints.invariant: reset_token.single_use and reset_token.expires_at <= now + 15m and reset_token.user_id == request.user_id and constant_time_compare(supplied, stored)
rule_constraints.precondition: recovery request is bound to a verified channel owned by the account
rule_constraints.postcondition: token invalidated atomically on first use; no password change without a valid unexpired token; identical responses for known and unknown accounts

text: Security invariant: ownership is derived exclusively from the authenticated principal and the server-side tenant context, never from request fields. Precondition: the principal is authenticated and authorized to create the resource. Postcondition: persisted owner_id and tenant_id equal the server-derived values, release or logout resets ownership atomically, and no chown or group change follows a user-controlled path. Filesystem creation should use a fixed service account, restrictive umask, and a path canonicalized under a controlled root. Periodic ownership audits detect drift.

metadata.title: CWE-708 Security Invariant: Ownership Assignment Tampering

rule_constraints.invariant: resource.owner_id = principal.id and resource.tenant_id = principal.tenant_id; ownership fields are never bound from request input
rule_constraints.precondition: principal is authenticated and resource creation is authorized
rule_constraints.postcondition: ownership persists server-derived values; release resets ownership atomically; no chown from user-controlled paths

text: Security invariant: every allocation surface has a server-enforced upper bound on size, count, and rate, scoped per principal and tenant. Precondition: the principal is authenticated and quota state is available. Postcondition: requests exceeding max_size, max_page, or the per-window quota are rejected with 413 or 429 before memory, database cursors, or persistent objects are allocated. Failures release partial allocations and fail closed. Quotas are enforced close to the resource, not only at the edge, and administrators can define and audit them.

metadata.title: CWE-770 Security Invariant: Unbounded Resource Allocation

rule_constraints.invariant: allocated_resources(principal, window) <= quota and request.size <= max_size and page_size <= max_page
rule_constraints.precondition: principal is authenticated and quota state is available
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject with 429 or 413 before allocation; fail closed; quotas enforced server-side per principal and tenant

text: Security invariant: a resource is released only after every reference is dropped and the associated transaction has committed. Precondition: acquisition creates a tracked lease with an owner and a reference count. Postcondition: release is idempotent but refused while references remain, pooled resources are scrubbed before reuse, stale handles fail closed, and locks are not released before commit or rollback. Lifecycle events are logged with correlation IDs so that early release can be detected in production.

metadata.title: CWE-826 Security Invariant: Premature Resource Release

rule_constraints.invariant: release(resource) only after reference_count == 0 and transaction_state == COMMITTED
rule_constraints.precondition: resource is acquired with a tracked lease
rule_constraints.postcondition: no reallocation before all references drop; stale handles fail closed; release is idempotent but not early

text: Security invariant: every state transition is an atomic compare-and-set or a serialized transaction, not an application-level check followed by a separate write. Precondition: the resource version or state is read inside the same transaction that performs the write. Postcondition: exactly one transition commits, all competing requests receive 409 or an equivalent conflict, and aggregate invariants such as ledger sum and inventory count remain valid. Uniqueness is enforced by a database constraint or idempotency key, and retries are safe.

metadata.title: CWE-362 Security Invariant: Race Condition and Concurrent State Mutation

rule_constraints.invariant: state transition is atomic: UPDATE ... WHERE version = expected_version AND used = false; affected_rows == 1
rule_constraints.precondition: resource state and version are read inside the same transaction
rule_constraints.postcondition: exactly one transition commits; all others receive 409; ledger sum equals the business invariant

text: Security invariant: the server independently recomputes every security-relevant value from authoritative state and never treats a client-computed value as authoritative. Precondition: the request contains a price, total, role, quantity, or file-type field that the client can influence. Postcondition: the persisted value equals the server-derived value, authorization uses server-side role state, and mismatches are rejected or overwritten rather than trusted. Client-side checks remain useful for UX and intrusion detection but never as the only control.

metadata.title: CWE-602 Security Invariant: Client-Side Control Bypass

rule_constraints.invariant: server recomputes price, total, role, and file type from authoritative state; client-supplied values are advisory only
rule_constraints.precondition: request contains a client-computed field
rule_constraints.postcondition: server-derived value is used for persistence and authorization; mismatch is rejected or ignored

text: Security invariant: authentication and authorization decisions are derived from server-side state or from tokens whose integrity is verified with a server-held key. Precondition: the request arrives from an untrusted client and may contain forged cookies, headers, or parameters. Postcondition: unsigned, malformed, or mismatched values are rejected, server-side session state is authoritative, and forwarding headers are ignored unless the immediate peer is a trusted proxy. JWT signatures, issuer, audience, and expiry are validated before any claim is used.

metadata.title: CWE-807 Security Invariant: Untrusted Input in Security Decisions

rule_constraints.invariant: security decisions use only server-side state or integrity-protected tokens verified with a server-held key
rule_constraints.precondition: request arrives from an untrusted client
rule_constraints.postcondition: unsigned or mismatched claims rejected; server state authoritative; proxy headers ignored unless from a trusted hop

text: Security invariant: any value that influences price, ownership, role, or workflow state is re-derived on the server from authoritative storage. Precondition: the request includes a hidden, readonly, cookie-based, or otherwise assumed-immutable parameter. Postcondition: the persisted value equals the server-derived value, and any client-supplied value is ignored, rejected, or integrity-checked with a server-held key. Hidden fields may carry opaque references but never authoritative prices, roles, or ownership.

metadata.title: CWE-472 Security Invariant: Assumed-Immutable Parameter Tampering

rule_constraints.invariant: server re-derives all security-relevant values from authoritative storage; client-submitted immutable fields are ignored or integrity-checked
rule_constraints.precondition: request includes a hidden or assumed-immutable parameter
rule_constraints.postcondition: persisted value equals the server-derived value; tampering is rejected or overwritten

text: Security invariant: request bodies are bound to explicit allowlisted DTOs, and privileged or internal attributes are never writable from client input. Precondition: the request body contains attributes for creation or update. Postcondition: only allowlisted fields are populated; unknown or privileged keys such as role, is_admin, balance, verified, and tenant_id are rejected or ignored; authorization state is unchanged. Create and update schemas are separate, and server-controlled fields are set exclusively by trusted code.

metadata.title: CWE-915 Security Invariant: Mass Assignment

rule_constraints.invariant: only explicitly allowed fields are bound; privileged fields are server-controlled and never mapped from request input
rule_constraints.precondition: request body contains attributes to create or update
rule_constraints.postcondition: allowlisted DTO populated; unknown or privileged keys rejected or ignored; role and balance unchanged

text: Security invariant: security-relevant comparisons use strict typed equality over canonicalized values, and secrets are compared in constant time. Precondition: both operands are validated for type, length, and canonical form. Postcondition: only exact, correctly typed equality grants access; prefixes, case variants, and coerced values are rejected; failures are uniform in timing and response. Role and entitlement comparisons use server-side identifiers, not display names, and null or missing values never compare equal to a valid value.

metadata.title: CWE-697 Security Invariant: Comparison Logic Bypass

rule_constraints.invariant: security comparisons use strict typed equality over canonicalized values; secrets use constant-time comparison; no substring or case-insensitive match for exact tokens
rule_constraints.precondition: both operands are validated and canonicalized
rule_constraints.postcondition: only exact, correctly typed equality grants access; failures are uniform in timing and response

text: Security invariant: every successful authentication or privilege elevation invalidates the existing session identifier and issues a new, server-generated one. Precondition: the user authenticates or steps up privileges. Postcondition: pre-authentication identifiers are rejected, URL-based session tracking is disabled, and cookies are set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite attributes. Session adoption endpoints require an authenticated, server-issued identifier and never accept one from an untrusted source. Logout and password change invalidate all sessions.

metadata.title: CWE-384 Security Invariant: Session Identifier Fixation

rule_constraints.invariant: session.id_after_auth != session.id_before_auth and session.authenticated implies session.issued_by_server_after_auth
rule_constraints.precondition: user authenticates or elevates privileges
rule_constraints.postcondition: all pre-auth identifiers invalidated; new identifier generated server-side; old identifier rejected

text: Security invariant: a password change requires proof of the current password or a fresh step-up authentication, plus a valid CSRF token. Precondition: the principal has an authenticated session. Postcondition: the new password is accepted only after successful verification, all other sessions are invalidated, and the change is audited. Administrative password changes require an explicit capability and a separate audit trail. Session possession alone is never sufficient proof of credential knowledge.

metadata.title: CWE-620 Security Invariant: Password Change Without Re-authentication

rule_constraints.invariant: password_change requires current_password_verified or step_up_auth_within_5m and csrf_token_valid
rule_constraints.precondition: principal has an authenticated session
rule_constraints.postcondition: new password set only after proof of current credential; all other sessions invalidated; audit event recorded

text: Security invariant: every expensive operation has an explicit cost bound, depth limit, timeout, and per-principal quota. Precondition: a request reaches a query, parser, report generator, or connection pool. Postcondition: the operation aborts at the configured limit, partial allocations are released, and the system fails closed rather than open. Connection pools have maximum sizes and idle timeouts, recursive parsers have depth limits, and database queries have statement timeouts and row caps.

metadata.title: CWE-400 Security Invariant: Resource Exhaustion Amplification

rule_constraints.invariant: cost(request) <= max_cost and depth(payload) <= max_depth and active_connections(principal) <= quota and timeout(op) <= max_time
rule_constraints.precondition: request reaches an expensive operation
rule_constraints.postcondition: operation aborts at the cost or depth limit; partial resources released; system fails closed; quotas enforced per principal

text: Security invariant: locks are acquired and released exactly once on every path, using a globally consistent order and a server-generated, non-predictable name. Precondition: a shared resource requires mutual exclusion. Postcondition: release occurs in a finally block and verifies ownership; acquisition has a timeout and deadlock detection; user input never determines a lock name or path. Predictable lock files are created with O_EXCL under a protected directory, and failed acquisition fails closed.

metadata.title: CWE-667 Security Invariant: Locking Discipline Failure

rule_constraints.invariant: lock.acquire() and lock.release() are paired in finally; lock order is global; lock names are server-generated and non-predictable; acquire has a timeout
rule_constraints.precondition: a shared resource requires mutual exclusion
rule_constraints.postcondition: locks released exactly once on every path; no deadlock beyond timeout; lock ownership verified before release

text: Security invariant: a security comparison evaluates every factor required by the decision, after canonicalizing the input into structured components. Precondition: the input is parsed into scheme, host, path, tenant, object, and type rather than compared as a raw string. Postcondition: the comparison is exact over all required factors, and missing or ambiguous factors fail closed. Path checks include a boundary, tenant checks include tenant_id, and allowlists use parsed values rather than substring matches.

metadata.title: CWE-1023 Security Invariant: Missing-Factor Comparison Bypass

rule_constraints.invariant: comparison includes every required factor: canonical scheme, canonical path with boundary, tenant_id, object_id, and type
rule_constraints.precondition: input is parsed and canonicalized into structured components
rule_constraints.postcondition: comparison is exact over all required factors; missing or ambiguous factors fail closed

text: Security invariant: a user-influenced path is decoded once, canonicalized with a platform function (realpath, getCanonicalPath, GetFullPath), and then compared against the canonical restricted root including a trailing separator boundary. Precondition: the path is derived from external input and must remain under a configured root. Postcondition: anything resolving outside the root, including symlink targets, is rejected with a uniform error, and the check happens after decoding so encoded and double-encoded forms cannot slip through. Where the acceptable set is known, replace free-form names with opaque identifiers mapped server-side. Run the service with least privilege and a filesystem sandbox.

metadata.title: CWE-22 Security Invariant: Path Traversal

rule_constraints.invariant: canonical(join(root, user_path)).startswith(canonical(root) + separator)
rule_constraints.precondition: the resolved path is derived from user input and must remain under a configured root
rule_constraints.postcondition: any resolved path outside the root is rejected after full canonicalization and symlink resolution; mapping tables used where the set is known

text: Security invariant: external programs are invoked through an API that separates the executable from an argument array, with shell interpretation disabled, and every user-influenced argument is validated against a strict allowlist or a strong type. Precondition: the application must invoke an external program. Postcondition: user data never reaches a shell string, leading dashes are rejected or separated with --, invalid arguments fail before invocation, and the process runs as a dedicated low-privilege account inside a sandbox. Where library equivalents exist, they replace external commands entirely. Output is captured and bounded, and invocations are audited.

metadata.title: CWE-78 Security Invariant: OS Command Injection

rule_constraints.invariant: subprocess is invoked with an argument array and shell=False; each argument is allowlisted or strict-typed; no user input reaches a shell string
rule_constraints.precondition: the application needs to invoke an external program
rule_constraints.postcondition: no shell interpretation of user data; invalid arguments rejected before invocation; process runs with least privilege and a sandbox

text: Security invariant: SQL values are always bound as parameters through prepared statements, and identifiers such as column and table names are selected from a server-side allowlist rather than interpolated. Precondition: a statement includes data influenced by an external actor. Postcondition: user input never becomes SQL syntax, dynamic identifiers resolve through a fixed map, database errors are generic and logged server-side, and the connection uses an account limited to the objects the feature needs. ORM raw fragments require review, and stored procedures avoid dynamic SQL internally. Escaping is defense in depth, never the primary control.

metadata.title: CWE-89 Security Invariant: SQL Injection

rule_constraints.invariant: every SQL value is bound through a prepared statement parameter; identifiers come from a server-side allowlist; the database account uses least privilege
rule_constraints.precondition: a SQL statement includes user-influenced data
rule_constraints.postcondition: user data never becomes SQL syntax; identifiers are mapped from a fixed set; errors are generic; the connection uses a least-privilege account

text: Security invariant: untrusted data is encoded for the exact output context before rendering, and client-side code never writes untrusted data into executable DOM sinks. Precondition: data influenced by an external actor is rendered into a page or assigned to a DOM property. Postcondition: HTML body, attribute, URL, JavaScript, and CSS contexts each receive their correct encoding; rich text passes through an allowlist sanitizer; session cookies are HttpOnly and Secure; and a strict Content-Security-Policy without unsafe-inline limits the impact of any missed sink. Framework auto-escaping is treated as the default, and every explicit bypass is reviewed.

metadata.title: CWE-79 Security Invariant: Cross-Site Scripting

rule_constraints.invariant: every output is contextually encoded for HTML body, attribute, URL, JavaScript, or CSS; DOM sinks receive only sanitized or trusted values; CSP restricts inline script
rule_constraints.precondition: untrusted data is rendered into a web page or written to a DOM sink
rule_constraints.postcondition: data is encoded for its exact context; script does not execute; CSP and HttpOnly limit impact if a sink is missed

text: Security invariant: data from untrusted sources is parsed with a data-only format and a strict schema, never with a native object deserializer. Precondition: the application must reconstruct structured data from external input. Postcondition: only allowlisted types are instantiated, serialized blobs are verified with an HMAC or signature before any parsing, and unsafe loaders such as pickle, BinaryFormatter, and yaml.load are replaced with safe equivalents. Deserialized values are treated as untrusted after reconstruction and revalidated. Where native serialization is unavoidable, a strict class allowlist and a hardened classpath limit gadget availability, and the component runs with least privilege.

metadata.title: CWE-502 Security Invariant: Insecure Deserialization

rule_constraints.invariant: only allowlisted classes are deserialized; serialized blobs are integrity-checked; untrusted input uses a data-only format such as JSON with strict schemas
rule_constraints.precondition: the application must reconstruct an object from external data
rule_constraints.postcondition: no arbitrary class instantiation; signature verified before deserialization; unsafe loaders replaced; failures reject the blob

text: Security invariant: every state-changing request must carry an unpredictable anti-CSRF token bound to the user's session and validated server-side, and the session cookie must use SameSite=Lax or Strict. Precondition: an authenticated browser issues a request that mutates state. Postcondition: requests lacking a valid token, or arriving with a disallowed Origin or Referer, are rejected before any mutation. Tokens are generated with a CSPRNG, compared in constant time, rotated on login, and never placed in URLs. Dangerous operations require a separate confirmation step, and GET handlers are strictly read-only.

metadata.title: CWE-352 Security Invariant: CSRF

rule_constraints.invariant: state_change requires valid csrf_token bound to session and (Origin in allowlist or SameSite=Lax/Strict cookie)
rule_constraints.precondition: an authenticated browser issues a state-changing request
rule_constraints.postcondition: requests without a valid token are rejected; tokens are unpredictable and session-bound; GET never mutates state

text: Security invariant: uploaded files are accepted only when their content matches an allowlist of safe types, determined by server-side sniffing and validated by re-encoding, and they are stored under a server-generated name in a non-executable location. Precondition: a file arrives from an untrusted actor. Postcondition: disallowed types are rejected, images are re-encoded to strip embedded payloads, filenames are generated with a CSPRNG and never derived from user input, storage sits outside the web root or in a directory with execution disabled, and files are served with Content-Disposition attachment and a correct Content-Type. Size, count, and archive-expansion limits apply.

metadata.title: CWE-434 Security Invariant: Unrestricted File Upload

rule_constraints.invariant: upload.type in allowlist determined by content sniffing and re-encoding; stored_name is server-generated; storage path is non-executable
rule_constraints.precondition: a file arrives from an untrusted actor
rule_constraints.postcondition: only allowed types persist; content is re-encoded or sanitized; files are served with a safe Content-Type and never executed

text: Security invariant: every XML parser that handles untrusted input disables DOCTYPE declarations, external entity resolution, and entity expansion, and enforces a schema that forbids these constructs. Precondition: the application parses XML from an untrusted source. Postcondition: documents declaring DTDs or external entities are rejected before parsing, parser-initiated file and network access is impossible, entity expansion limits prevent billion-laughs exhaustion, and errors do not reveal resolved content. Egress filtering blocks parser-originated traffic to internal ranges, and XML libraries are pinned and reviewed for safe defaults.

metadata.title: CWE-611 Security Invariant: XML External Entity Injection

rule_constraints.invariant: xml_parser.disallow_doctype and xml_parser.resolve_external_entities == false and xml_parser.expand_entities == false
rule_constraints.precondition: the application parses XML from an untrusted source
rule_constraints.postcondition: DTDs and external entities are rejected; no parser-initiated file or network access occurs; errors are generic

text: Security invariant: server-side fetches are restricted to an explicit allowlist of destinations, validated after DNS resolution against private, loopback, link-local, and metadata ranges, with every redirect hop revalidated. Precondition: the server fetches a URL influenced by an external actor. Postcondition: disallowed destinations fail closed before any connection, DNS rebinding is defeated by pinning the resolved address, egress policy blocks internal ranges at the network layer, and response size and content type are bounded. Fetched content is never returned raw to the user, and webhook destinations require ownership verification.

metadata.title: CWE-918 Security Invariant: SSRF

rule_constraints.invariant: resolved_ip(url) not in private_or_linklocal_or_metadata_ranges and each redirect hop revalidated and response size bounded
rule_constraints.precondition: the server fetches a URL influenced by an external actor
rule_constraints.postcondition: only allowlisted destinations are reachable; redirects revalidated; egress blocked to internal ranges; response not returned raw

text: Security invariant: regular expressions applied to untrusted input avoid nested or overlapping quantifiers, are anchored and unambiguous, and run under an explicit input-length cap, backtracking limit, and execution-time budget. Precondition: a regex processes input influenced by an external actor. Postcondition: matching completes within a bounded time regardless of input shape, pathological inputs are truncated or rejected before matching, and a timeout aborts the operation without wedging a worker. Prefer non-backtracking engines or linear-time parsers for complex grammars, and test every pattern against adversarial strings in CI.

metadata.title: CWE-1333 Security Invariant: ReDoS

rule_constraints.invariant: regex has no nested quantifiers over the same class and input length <= max_len and backtrack_limit and time_budget configured
rule_constraints.precondition: a regex processes input influenced by an external actor
rule_constraints.postcondition: matching completes within a bounded time; pathological inputs are truncated or rejected; a timeout aborts the match

text: Security invariant: every credential-bearing request uses TLS with a valid certificate, and no authentication flow can be downgraded to HTTP. Precondition: the user submits a password, OTP, reset token, or session credential. Postcondition: the request is encrypted end to end, the response sets Strict-Transport-Security, and all session cookies carry Secure and HttpOnly. Redirects preserve the scheme, form actions are relative or HTTPS, and content security policy forbids mixed active content. HSTS preload and certificate pinning are defense in depth for high-value identity providers.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-01: Encrypted-Only Authentication Invariant

rule_constraints.transport: request.scheme == https for every authentication, reset, and token endpoint
rule_constraints.mixed_content: no active content loaded over http on an https page

text: Security invariant: no account in any environment can authenticate with a vendor-supplied or documented default credential. Precondition: a component is provisioned or an installer completes. Postcondition: the first login forces a unique strong credential, demo and integration accounts are disabled by default, and every account has an owner and rotation record. Administrative interfaces are bound to a management network or protected by a bastion, and authentication attempts with known default pairs raise an alert. Provisioning pipelines scan for default hashes before promotion.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-02: No-Shared-Default Invariant

rule_constraints.first_login: must_change_password == true and cannot be skipped
rule_constraints.inventory: every account has an accountable owner and rotation record
rule_constraints.exposure: administrative interfaces not reachable from untrusted networks
rule_constraints.detection: failed default-pair attempts alert within 5 minutes

text: Security invariant: authentication attempts are bounded per account and per source over a sliding window, with progressive delay, risk-based challenges, and a safe unlock path. Precondition: a client submits credentials. Postcondition: after a small number of failures the account requires a delay, CAPTCHA, MFA, or temporary lock, and the legitimate owner is notified with a self-service unlock. Counters are server-side, survive new sessions, and aggregate across IPs and headers. Lockout never becomes a permanent denial-of-service primitive, and successful authentication resets only the relevant counter.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-03: Bounded Authentication Attempt Invariant

rule_constraints.per_account: failed_attempts within window <= 5 before progressive delay or lock
rule_constraints.per_source: distributed attempts aggregated by device and network signals
rule_constraints.recovery: lockout uses time-based unlock plus notification, not permanent denial

text: Security invariant: every route is denied by default and reachable only through an explicit server-side authorization policy applied uniformly across methods, path encodings, hosts, and ports. Precondition: a request arrives for any application route. Postcondition: unauthenticated requests are redirected or rejected before the handler runs, and no client-supplied flag, header, or parameter can establish identity. Route inventories are generated from the framework and tested in CI for unauthenticated access, and the auth middleware is attached at the router level rather than per handler.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-04: Default-Deny Route Authorization Invariant

rule_constraints.default: deny unless an explicit policy grants the route
rule_constraints.enforcement: server-side middleware applied to every route, method, and host
rule_constraints.identity: authorization uses server-side session state only
rule_constraints.coverage: route inventory tested in CI for unauthenticated access

text: Security invariant: persistent login uses an opaque, high-entropy selector and validator pair stored server-side and bound to a device or series, never the password or a predictable derivation. Precondition: a user selects remember-me. Postcondition: the cookie contains only the selector and validator, each use rotates the validator, reuse of an old validator invalidates the whole series, and logout or password change revokes every token. Cookies are HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, and scoped to the authentication path with a bounded lifetime.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-05: Rotating Bound Persistent-Token Invariant

rule_constraints.storage: opaque random selector and validator; never the password
rule_constraints.binding: token bound to device fingerprint or server-side series
rule_constraints.rotation: validator rotated on each use; reuse invalidates the series
rule_constraints.revocation: logout and password change revoke all persistent tokens

text: Security invariant: every response that contains authenticated, personal, or one-time data is marked no-store and must not be retained by browsers or shared caches. Precondition: the response is generated for an authenticated session or contains a secret. Postcondition: the response carries Cache-Control no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate and Pragma no-cache, personalized cacheable responses include Vary: Cookie and Authorization, and shared proxies are configured not to store authenticated bodies. Sensitive form fields disable autocomplete, and logout invalidates both server and client state.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-06: No-Store Policy for Sensitive Responses

rule_constraints.headers: Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate; Pragma: no-cache
rule_constraints.vary: Vary: Cookie, Authorization on any cacheable personalized response
rule_constraints.proxy: shared caches must not store Set-Cookie or authenticated bodies
rule_constraints.autocomplete: autocomplete=off on sensitive fields and one-time codes

text: Security invariant: passwords are at least twelve characters, screened against breached and common password lists plus application-specific context words, and accepted only through server-side enforcement. Precondition: a user creates, changes, or resets a password. Postcondition: weak, breached, and context-derived passwords are rejected with actionable guidance, passphrases and all printable characters are allowed, and there is no forced composition rule that produces predictable variants. The policy applies equally to API and direct requests, and MFA is available independently of password strength.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-07: Strong Password and Breach-Screening Invariant

rule_constraints.blocklist: reject top breached and common passwords and context words
rule_constraints.composition: no forced complexity rules; allow passphrases and all characters
rule_constraints.enforcement: server-side on create, change, and reset

text: Security invariant: account recovery relies on a verified channel the user controls, such as email, push approval, or a hardware key, rather than static personal facts. Precondition: a user requests recovery. Postcondition: recovery requires a single-use, short-lived token delivered to a verified channel, any additional challenge is rate-limited, and recovery cannot bypass MFA without a second proof. Where legacy questions remain, answers are treated as low-entropy secrets with strict limits, constant-time comparison, and mandatory notification.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-08: No-Static-Knowledge Recovery Invariant

rule_constraints.primary: recovery uses a verified channel such as email or push, not static facts
rule_constraints.rate_limit: 5 attempts per account per hour on any challenge
rule_constraints.impact: recovery never bypasses MFA without additional proof

text: Security invariant: reset tokens are single-use, short-lived, bound to the account, and compared in constant time, and password changes require proof of the current credential. Precondition: a user requests a reset or changes a password. Postcondition: the token is invalidated atomically on first use, the reset host comes from configuration rather than request headers, the change requires the current password or a fresh step-up, and every other session is invalidated. Responses are identical for known and unknown accounts.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-09: Single-Use Bound Reset Invariant

rule_constraints.token: single-use, 15-minute lifetime, bound to user and request
rule_constraints.compare: constant-time comparison of a hashed token
rule_constraints.host: reset host fixed by configuration, never from Host or X-Forwarded-Host
rule_constraints.change: requires current password or fresh step-up; all sessions invalidated

text: Security invariant: every channel that authenticates an identity enforces the same factor requirements, risk checks, and session protections as the primary flow. Precondition: a user authenticates through web, mobile, API, IVR, or support. Postcondition: no channel can issue a session with fewer factors than the account policy requires, support resets require strong verification and are audited, and cross-channel anomalies are correlated. A single policy decision point governs all channels, and new channels are reviewed against the same baseline before launch.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-10: Uniform Cross-Channel Authentication Invariant

rule_constraints.parity: every channel enforces the same factors and risk checks
rule_constraints.identity: one identity store and one policy decision point
rule_constraints.support: agent-initiated reset requires strong verification and audit

text: Security invariant: session identifiers are opaque, at least 128 bits from a cryptographic random source, and map to server-side state that the client cannot read or modify. Precondition: a session is created or resumed. Postcondition: the identifier carries no user data and no predictable structure, client-side state is signed or encrypted, idle and absolute timeouts apply, and the identifier rotates on authentication and privilege change. Validation fails closed for unknown or expired identifiers.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-01: High-Entropy Server-Side Session Invariant

rule_constraints.storage: server-side state keyed by opaque identifier
rule_constraints.integrity: client-side state signed or encrypted; never trusted raw
rule_constraints.lifecycle: idle and absolute timeouts; rotation on privilege change

text: Security invariant: session and authentication cookies are issued with Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Lax or Strict, scoped to the narrowest host and path, with a bounded lifetime. Precondition: the server sets a cookie containing a session or credential. Postcondition: the cookie cannot be read by script, is not sent over cleartext, is not attached to cross-site requests unless explicitly intended, and is not shared with sibling applications. The __Host- prefix is used where feasible, and cookie configuration is tested in CI.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-02: Hardened Session Cookie Invariant

rule_constraints.secure: Secure on every session and auth cookie
rule_constraints.httponly: HttpOnly on all cookies not required by JavaScript
rule_constraints.samesite: Lax or Strict; None only with Secure and explicit need

text: Security invariant: authentication and privilege elevation invalidate the existing identifier and issue a new server-generated one, and identifiers are never accepted from URLs or untrusted cookies. Precondition: a user logs in or elevates privileges. Postcondition: the pre-authentication identifier is rejected, the new identifier is set only by the server, URL-based tracking is disabled, and session adoption requires a server-issued authenticated identifier. Logout and password change invalidate all associated sessions.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-03: Authentication-Boundary Rotation Invariant

rule_constraints.rotation: new identifier on login, privilege change, and impersonation
rule_constraints.transport: identifier only in Secure HttpOnly cookies; never in URLs
rule_constraints.adoption: no session adoption from untrusted input

text: Security invariant: session and reset tokens are confined to Secure HttpOnly cookies or Authorization headers and never appear in URLs, logs, hidden fields, or third-party-reachable channels. Precondition: the application issues or consumes a token. Postcondition: tokens are absent from query strings, paths, and referrers, logging redacts sensitive headers, and third-party resources cannot observe them. A strict Referrer-Policy and a content security policy limit leakage, and hidden fields carry only opaque references bound to the server-side session.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-04: Token Confinement Invariant

rule_constraints.transport: session tokens only in Secure HttpOnly cookies
rule_constraints.logging: never log tokens, passwords, or Authorization headers
rule_constraints.urls: no secrets in query strings or paths

text: Security invariant: every state-changing request carries a valid anti-CSRF token bound to the session, and the session cookie uses SameSite=Lax or Strict with Origin or Referer validation as defense in depth. Precondition: an authenticated browser issues a mutating request. Postcondition: requests without a valid token or from a disallowed origin are rejected, GET handlers never mutate state, and sensitive operations require re-confirmation. Tokens are CSPRNG-generated, constant-time compared, and rotated on login.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-05: Intent-Verified State Change Invariant

rule_constraints.token: unpredictable per-session or per-request token validated server-side
rule_constraints.samesite: Lax or Strict on session cookies
rule_constraints.origin: Origin or Referer checked for state-changing requests

text: Security invariant: logout invalidates the server-side session record and every token derived from it, and the operation itself is protected against CSRF. Precondition: a user invokes logout.
